what: ATL @ MIL quarter scores contradict the printed final
why: The game book SCORE BY PERIOD table prints Milwaukee Q3 as 37 (quarters sum 116), while the printed final is 106 and the same document's recap line prints 27 in Q3 (sums to 106).
impact: One result row withheld from settlement. Nothing else reads it: the model excludes withheld games.

what: NYK @ TOR recap line is truncated
why: The recap prints "RAPTORS 17 26" - two values where six are expected. The period table sums to the printed 108 in overtime, so the row is settled on the period table.
impact: None on settlement; the truncation is recorded on the row.

what: Jimmy Butler III (GSW) row has no printed status
why: The PDF text layer prints no Current Status cell for this row; the Reason text occupies the status position.
impact: Status published as blank. It is not copied from the 11/15 report, because that would be an inference.

what: 15 team rows in the injury report read NOT YET SUBMITTED
why: Clubs that had not filed when the 09:15 AM ET report was produced are listed with a placeholder, not with players.
impact: No player is implied by a placeholder. The teams are shown on the injuries page.

what: 7 injury rows arrive with a blank TEAM cell
why: The table continues across a page break and the extractor loses the team cell for the continuation rows.
impact: Each was attributed from the printed row immediately above it in the same game block, and the evidence is stored on the row and shown as an "attributed" tag on the injuries page.

what: Two game books contain player rows with dropped cells
why: DAL@BOS Walter Clayton Jr. has no PTS cell; Morez Johnson Jr. has no BS cell; OKC@SAC Adaya Mara's row is misaligned.
impact: The affected player rows are rejected by the PTS and rebound identity checks and are not used. Team totals are unaffected.

why: The closing-lines artefact records a feed status of "not connected".
impact: The market-anchored prior is null on every line and both the naive and the model price are published without a market comparison.

what: No strategy can be funded at this sample size
why: No team has four captured games, which is the floor this build sets before it will treat a z-score as meaningful.
impact: 0 of 25 strategies published. Every row on the strategy board carries its block reason.

what: POR @ MIN appears twice in the window
why: Portland and Minnesota play on both 11/16 and 11/17. Both are genuine official fixtures with distinct game IDs; neither is a duplicate capture.
impact: Both rows are published. The repeated pairing is noted so it is not mistaken for a double-count.

what: Two 11/17 fixtures start after midnight UTC
why: UTA@LAC (10:30 ET) and CHA@LAL (11:00 ET) on 11/17 begin on 11/18 in UTC.
impact: Dates on this site are the league's Eastern-time game dates, not UTC dates. Stated so a reader comparing with a UTC log is not surprised.

what: Travel distance uses a secondary coordinate source
why: Arena coordinates come from each building's Wikipedia article, not from an NBA document. Distances are great-circle, which is a lower bound on travel.
impact: Travel cells are labelled secondary and every distance names its article. Missing coordinates print as blank.

what: Estimator A is overconfident on a 22-game log
why: Leave-one-game-out selected the smallest ridge tested (0.1), which produces 22-35 point margins from one or two games per team. The selection curve is monotone in the wrong direction because LOO on 22 games rewards an under-regularised fit.
impact: A's raw rating is published but labelled not-yet-publishable as a standalone line; every line shows A, B and the disagreement, and the confidence pill is driven by the disagreement.

why: The official game books print per-player lines but this round captured only team totals.
impact: Player-prop parlay prices are withheld entirely; no minutes-redistribution or replacement-share number is published.

what: DET PACE and POSS/GP differ by more than two possessions
why: On the official advanced page DET prints PACE 99.48 while POSS/GP is 101.42. Other teams reconcile within ~1.5. The difference is consistent with a large overtime count, since PACE is computed on regulation-adjusted possessions.
impact: The totals model uses the printed PACE, not POSS/GP. Recorded because the two do not agree as tightly as for other teams.

what: One gate fails, and it is scoped to a single row
why: I2_quarter_scores fails on 0022600243 (ATL@MIL) because the quarters do not sum to the printed final. It is scoped "row", so it withholds that row rather than blocking the rebuild.
impact: 13 of 14 gates pass; no build-scoped gate fails; the rebuild is allowed.
